obligation: HIPAA Security Rule: Care Delivery
applies: Yes (covered entity; also a business associate of 38 practices)
basis: A health care provider that sends claims and eligibility as standard electronic transactions is a covered entity (45 CFR 160.103). Care Delivery hosts SYS-D4 for 38 white-label practices, which makes it their business associate. No size exemption; 164.306(b) affects how, not whether

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule: Health Plan
basis: A health plan is a covered entity; the definition of health plan in 45 CFR 160.103 lists the Medicare Advantage program. Care Delivery and the Health Plan are separate subsidiaries with no affiliated covered entity designation, so each is a separate covered entity (45 CFR 164.105(b)); group legal confirmed this on 2026-08-14

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule: Health-Tech SaaS
basis: The SaaS creates, receives, maintains and transmits ePHI for about 420 covered-entity customers under BAAs, so it is a business associate directly subject to the Security Rule

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule: corporate shared services
basis: Corporate shared services in the parent creates, receives, maintains and transmits both covered entities' ePHI on SYS-G1 to SYS-G3 under intercompany BAAs

obligation: HIPAA Privacy Rule: Care Delivery
basis: Covered entity. PHI sent to the Health Plan is a disclosure between separate covered entities and needs a permission such as 164.506(c) and minimum necessary (164.502(b), 164.514(d))

obligation: HIPAA Privacy Rule: Health Plan
basis: Covered entity. Minimum-necessary protocols for routine disclosures (164.514(d)(3)); TPO disclosures with Care Delivery (164.506(c))

obligation: HIPAA Privacy Rule: Health-Tech SaaS
basis: A business associate may use PHI only as its BAAs permit; 97 BAAs signed before 2022 do not expressly permit de-identification

obligation: HIPAA Privacy Rule: corporate shared services
basis: Uses and disclosures limited to the intercompany BAAs; de-identification under 164.514(b)

obligation: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule: Care Delivery
basis: Own notices to individuals, HHS and media as a covered entity; notices to the 38 practices as their business associate

obligation: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule: Health Plan
basis: Own notices as a separate covered entity

obligation: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule: Health-Tech SaaS
basis: Notice to each affected customer under 164.410 and the BAA terms (10 calendar days standard; 72 hours for 42 customers)

obligation: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule: corporate shared services
basis: Notice to both covered entities as their business associate

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule NPRM (2025): all divisions and group
basis: Not a final rule; tracked for planning

obligation: 42 CFR Part 2 (SUD records): all divisions and group
basis: No division operates a federally assisted substance use disorder program

obligation: FTC Health Breach Notification Rule: all divisions and group
basis: 16 CFR 318.1 excludes HIPAA covered entities and business associates acting as such; every division acts as one or the other

obligation: Section 1557 patient care decision support tools: Care Delivery
basis: Care Delivery receives federal financial assistance through Medicare and Medicaid; the AI scribe and predictive decision support are in use

obligation: Section 1557 patient care decision support tools: Health Plan
applies: Applied as a precaution (under counsel review)
basis: Medicare Advantage payments are federal financial assistance under 45 CFR 92.4; whether UM tools support clinical decision-making is under counsel review; the UM model uses age and disability status

obligation: Section 1557 patient care decision support tools: Health-Tech SaaS
basis: The SaaS does not use the feature in its own health programs; customers that use it may ask for tool information

obligation: CMS emergency preparedness: Care Delivery ASCs
basis: ASCs are a certified provider type with an emergency preparedness condition for coverage. 42 CFR 482.15 does not apply because the group operates no hospitals

obligation: CMS emergency preparedness: Health Plan, SaaS and group
basis: None of these is a certified provider type

obligation: HIPAA applicability to social assistance: all divisions and group
basis: No division is a social assistance organization
The Health Plan holds a Medicare Advantage contract and uses an AI model in utilization management. Not applicable to Care Delivery, the SaaS or the group

obligation: GLBA privacy and safeguards: Health Plan
basis: The Health Plan is an insurer holding member nonpublic personal information; state insurance authorities enforce GLBA for insurers (15 U.S.C. 6805(a)(6)). Not applicable to the other divisions

obligation: NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law #668: Health Plan
citation: NAIC Model #668 as enacted by each state
basis: The Health Plan is a licensee in 6 states; duties apply where a state has enacted the model, and text varies by state

obligation: NYDFS Cybersecurity Regulation: all divisions
basis: No division holds a New York insurance license

obligation: Bank and credit union security rules: all divisions
citation: 12 CFR 30 App. B; 12 CFR Part 748; 12 CFR Part 30 App. D
basis: No division holds a bank or credit union charter

obligation: SEC cybersecurity disclosure (also N51-R08): group
basis: The holding company is an SEC registrant; divisions contribute incident facts through the group

obligation: FTC Act Section 5: all divisions and group
applies: Yes (SaaS, Care Delivery and group; limited for the Health Plan)
basis: Unfair or deceptive security and AI claims; most insurance activity is outside FTC jurisdiction

obligation: DOJ Data Security Program: all divisions and group
basis: The group holds personal health data above the bulk thresholds; vendor and contractor access must be screened

obligation: FedRAMP: Health-Tech SaaS
basis: No federal agency customers

obligation: COPPA Rule: Health-Tech SaaS and patient app
basis: No child-directed service

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (breach notification): all divisions
basis: The group holds personal information of Florida residents; other states' breach laws apply where affected individuals reside (Florida is the worked example)

obligation: Intercompany BAAs: corporate shared services with each covered entity
basis: Care Delivery BAA (2024) and Health Plan BAA (2019) set corporate's permitted uses and notice duties

obligation: SaaS customer BAAs and master agreements: Health-Tech SaaS
basis: Standard BAA notice clocks (10 calendar days for breaches; 5 business days for other incidents; 72 hours for 42 customers) and de-identification terms

obligation: SOC 2 Type 2 commitments: Health-Tech SaaS and the Care Delivery patient-app platform
citation: AICPA Trust Services Criteria; customer contracts
applies: Yes (SaaS annually); planned for the patient-app platform; Health Plan out of scope
basis: SaaS customers rely on the annual report; the 38 white-label practices asked for a report by the end of 2027
